about: The one place where Ritual's groups and packages are defined. Groups: what you were doing when the mistake happened (every lesson has one). Packages: what kind of project you are building (only for lessons that apply to that kind alone). `covers` is what decides where a lesson goes; `detect` lists the dependencies that turn a package on at setup. See lessons/TEMPLATE.md#where-a-lesson-goes before adding one.

groups.covers: Writing for people: documentation, manuals, screen text, content, prompts.
Calculating, measuring or showing a number: dashboards, reports, models, metrics, queries.
Checking something: automated tests, validators, reviews, calibration.
A program that writes, generates, transforms or moves files and data.
Something a person will see or use: screens, components, styles, pages, forms.
Running commands, servers, tests or captures, and the tool that gets between you and the system.
Saving, closing, handing off or coordinating: commits, states, pending items, parallel work.

web.covers: Websites and web front ends: pages, forms, components, styles, what runs in the browser and the small server behind a site.

apps.covers: Applications with a backend of their own: APIs, authentication, databases, payments, background jobs.

crm.covers: Customer systems and messaging: CRMs, email and SMS sending, contact lists, sales pipelines.

ai.covers: Products built on language models, and models trained or fine-tuned on your own examples: prompts, agents, retrieval, evaluations, model calls, training data.

security.covers: What does not visibly break: secrets, access, input from outside, data exposure. Only `proposal` lessons with a public source, or lessons confirmed in the field.

education.covers: Projects that teach: courses, lessons, exercises, quizzes, tutorials and the platforms that deliver and grade them.

video.covers: Videos, screencasts and animations built with code: scenes, narration, subtitles, timing and render.
